action: Operators of Quantum Systems drones: follow the company's and your authority's guidance before flying, and do not install software updates until the company confirms they are safe.
exec: A cyberattack on a defence supplier has taken military equipment out of service, showing supplier risk reaching operations.
plain: German drone maker Quantum Systems confirmed a cyberattack, noticed in late October, that disrupted its operations. Reports say attackers may have used a malicious software update, and the German military stopped using the company's drones.
summary: Quantum Systems confirmed an active cyberattack by "hostile actors", noticed at the end of October, that disrupted operations. Der Spiegel and the Financial Times, as relayed by Security Affairs and Euronews, report attackers may have used a malicious update, and that the German military stopped using its drones. No attacker is named and details are not officially confirmed.
title: German military grounds Quantum Systems drones after cyberattack on the maker

validation.note: Security Affairs (Nov 16) and Euronews (Nov 13) both relay the company statement and Spiegel/FT reporting. The malicious update is reported as possible, not confirmed.

date_note: Company confirmed the attack publicly on November 12-13 (Euronews, November 13); Security Affairs covered it on November 16.

review.note: Checked against Security Affairs and Euronews (Spiegel/FT relay). Date moved from Nov 16 to Nov 13 (company went public); update wording made 'reported/possible'; Euronews added as second publisher; plain no longer states the update as fact. Correction file added.
